q: How does a newspaper printing plant work out carbon per copy?
title: Newspaper printing: carbon per copy
short: Add newsprint and ink as purchased goods to the plant's own electricity and fuel, then divide by copies printed. Newsprint usually dominates, so the paper mill's figure per tonne matters more than anything on the press floor.
audience: Newspaper printing centres in India running web offset presses

ul: Newsprint: tonnes used, including waste, times the mill's factor per tonne. Scope 3 category 1.
Ink and plates: kilograms and plates used times supplier factors.
Press hall electricity and any diesel generator use: Scope 2 and Scope 1.
Copies printed, from the circulation run sheets.

p: Start up waste and unsold returns use paper too. Count newsprint consumed, not paper in copies sold.
Ask the mill. Recycled fibre newsprint and virgin newsprint differ widely, so a generic number can be far off.
